stem: A team is designing a read-scaling plan for an Aurora MySQL cluster and wants to confirm the current mechanics and limits of Aurora Replicas before committing to the design. Which TWO statements about Aurora Replicas are accurate? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: A single Aurora cluster can have up to 15 Aurora Replicas
The cluster's reader endpoint automatically load-balances connections across the Aurora Replicas
Aurora Replicas are only supported in a different Region than the primary
Aurora Replicas each maintain a separate full copy of the data, doubling storage per replica
An Aurora Replica can only be added to or removed from a cluster by stopping the cluster

rationale: An Aurora cluster supports up to 15 Aurora Replicas, and the reader endpoint automatically load-balances connections across whichever of them are currently healthy, both accurate mechanics of the feature. Aurora Replicas are commonly created in the same Region as the primary, so restricting them to a different Region is incorrect. They share the primary's underlying cluster storage rather than each holding a separate full copy, so they do not double storage per replica. Adding or removing an Aurora Replica does not require stopping the cluster.
